newsitem.title: CHINA: Strong quake in northwest China kills three.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake in northwest China kills three.

text.p: A strong earthquake jolted northwest China on Friday, killing at least three people and injuring several in an area rocked by thousands of tremors in recent weeks, officials said.
The earthquake measuring 6.6 on the Richter scale struck Jiashi in the northwestern Xinjiang region at 1.34 p.m. (0534 GMT), a local official said by telephone.
"This earthquake was very sudden," the official said by telephone from Jiashi. "We had no preparation."
At least three people had been killed and many buildings were destroyed by the latest tremor, which caused severe damage, officials and the Xinhua news agency said.
Hospital officials said several people had been injured, but no precise figures were available yet.

"There have been so many earthquakes here recently that no one dares to go home and we are all living in tents," one hospital official said. "The casualties this time were because buildings collapsed on tents nearby.
"The earth never seems to stop shaking," she said. "But today the earthquake felt even stronger than before."
Two large earthquakes just five hours apart rocked Jiashi last Sunday, injuring 23 people and destroying thousands of buildings, officials said.
The first earthquake last Sunday measured 6.3 on the open-ended Richter scale and it was followed by a stronger tremor of magnitude 6.4 just five hours later.

No deaths were reported from Sunday's tremors in Jiashi, mainly because most residents have been living out of doors and in tents since an earthquake measuring 6.4 rocked Jiashi in January, killing 50 people, officials said.

More than 4,000 earthquakes and aftershocks have jolted the region that is populated mainly by cotton farmers and sheep herders since January, and seismologists have warned of more tremors in the region.
On March 20, an earthquake measuring 6.9 hit Jiashi, killing 24 people and injuring 40. That came just days after a tremor of 6.0 magnitude left two people dead and injured three.
Many of the region's residents live in earthen houses that are easily damaged by earthquakes.
Chinese scientist Ding Jianhai forecast earlier on Friday that Jiashi would be jolted soon by an earthquake of about five on the Richter scale, Xinhua reported.
"The quakes hitting the area have shown no obvious signs of decline in terms of magnitude in the near future," it quoted Ding, a research fellow with the State Seismological Bureau, as saying.

Officials said it was rare in seismological history that so many strong quakes should hit in the same place at such short intervals, said Ding, head of the Department of Earthquake Prediction and Analysis.
Chinese seismolgists had agreed that the earthquakes were not an isolated phenomenon and were linked to the fact that China has entered a period of high seismological activity.
In 1961, three earthquakes measuring more than six on the Richter scale jolted Jiashi, and after-shocks continued for 20 months, he said.
